title: Ancient Egypt
intro: Pyramids, pharaohs and hieroglyphs. Step back thousands of years along the River Nile.

questions.prompt: Along which river did ancient Egyptian life grow up?
questions.explanation: The Nile flooded each year and left rich soil for farming, so most ancient Egyptians lived along its banks.

questions.prompt: What were the kings of ancient Egypt called?
questions.explanation: The rulers of ancient Egypt were called pharaohs.

questions.prompt: What do we call the ancient Egyptian writing made of pictures and symbols?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphs used hundreds of picture symbols to stand for sounds, words and ideas.

questions.prompt: Tutankhamun became pharaoh when he was still a child.
questions.explanation: Tutankhamun was only about nine years old when he became pharaoh.

questions.prompt: Who led the team that found Tutankhamun's tomb?
questions.explanation: The archaeologist Howard Carter found the tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

questions.prompt: In which year was Tutankhamun's tomb discovered?
questions.explanation: Howard Carter's team discovered the tomb in November 1922, still filled with treasure.

questions.prompt: What did the ancient Egyptians make to preserve the bodies of people who had died?
questions.explanation: They dried and wrapped bodies to make mummies, because they believed the body was needed in the afterlife.

questions.prompt: What were the great pyramids at Giza built as?
questions.explanation: The pyramids were built as tombs for pharaohs.

questions.prompt: The ancient Egyptians made a kind of paper from papyrus reeds.
questions.explanation: Papyrus reeds grew along the Nile, and their stems were pressed into sheets for writing on.

questions.prompt: Which huge stone statue at Giza has the body of a lion and the head of a human?
questions.explanation: The Great Sphinx lies near the pyramids at Giza. It was carved from the rock with a lion's body and a human head.

questions.prompt: Which famous stone helped experts finally work out how to read hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone has the same message carved in three scripts. Because scholars could read the Greek, they could work out the hieroglyphs.

questions.prompt: In which museum can you see the Rosetta Stone today?
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone has been on display at the British Museum in London since 1802.

questions.prompt: Which French scholar made the big breakthrough in reading Egyptian hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: Jean-François Champollion studied the Rosetta Stone and, in 1822, showed how hieroglyphs could be read.

questions.prompt: Which famous queen is known as the last pharaoh of ancient Egypt?
questions.explanation: Cleopatra VII was the last pharaoh to rule ancient Egypt. After her reign, Egypt became part of the Roman Empire.

questions.prompt: Ra was the ancient Egyptian god of what?
questions.explanation: Ra was the sun god, one of the most important gods in ancient Egypt. He was often shown with the head of a falcon.

questions.prompt: Which animal did many ancient Egyptian families keep as a pet and treat as sacred?
questions.explanation: Cats were sacred to the ancient Egyptians. Many families kept one, believing it would bring the household good luck.

questions.prompt: Why was the yearly flooding of the Nile good for Egyptian farmers?

options.label: It left behind rich, fertile soil
It brought fish into the fields

questions.explanation: When the Nile flooded, it left a layer of dark, fertile mud on the land, perfect for growing crops like wheat and barley.

questions.prompt: The largest pyramid at Giza was built for which pharaoh?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was built for the pharaoh Khufu. It is the largest of all the Egyptian pyramids.

questions.prompt: During mummification, what were canopic jars used for?
questions.explanation: Embalmers removed organs such as the lungs and stomach and kept them in special containers called canopic jars, buried with the mummy.

questions.prompt: In which valley were many pharaohs, including Tutankhamun, buried?
questions.explanation: The Valley of the Kings, near the ancient city of Thebes, holds the tombs of many New Kingdom pharaohs.

questions.prompt: What famous object was found covering the head of Tutankhamun's mummy?
questions.explanation: Tutankhamun's golden burial mask is one of the most famous treasures ever found. It is made of gold and precious stones.

questions.prompt: Which Egyptian god ruled over the afterlife and is often shown wrapped like a mummy?
questions.explanation: Osiris was the god of the dead and the afterlife. Pictures often show him wrapped like a mummy and wearing a tall white crown.

questions.prompt: The Egyptian god Anubis is usually shown with the head of which animal?
questions.explanation: Anubis had the head of a jackal, a wild dog. He was the god who looked after the process of mummification.

questions.prompt: What were the people called whose job was to read and write hieroglyphs?
questions.explanation: Scribes trained for years to learn hundreds of signs. They kept records, wrote letters and copied important texts.

questions.prompt: What was Senet, which ancient Egyptians enjoyed for more than 2,000 years?
questions.explanation: Senet was a board game. Players threw sticks, a bit like dice, to see how many squares to move their pieces.

questions.prompt: In ancient Egypt, both men and women wore eye make-up.
questions.explanation: Men and women both wore eye paint, usually green or black. They thought it protected their eyes from the sun and had healing powers.

questions.prompt: Hatshepsut was a woman who ruled ancient Egypt as pharaoh.
questions.explanation: Hatshepsut was one of only a few female pharaohs. She ruled for about 20 years and built grand temples.

questions.prompt: The River Nile flows from south to north.
questions.explanation: The Nile flows north into the Mediterranean Sea. That is why southern Egypt was called Upper Egypt and northern Egypt Lower Egypt.

questions.prompt: Roughly how many years ago was the Great Pyramid of Giza built?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was built around 2500 BC, which is about 4,500 years ago.

questions.prompt: The ancient Egyptians believed in more than how many gods and goddesses?
questions.explanation: The ancient Egyptians believed in more than 2,000 gods and goddesses, with gods for almost everything in daily life.
